status_note: Promoted on 2026-09-25 as the E29 reference; cluster.env.example mounts both files with VLLM_E29_END_DRAIN=1, VLLM_E29_IDLE_COALESCE_MS=4 and VLLM_E29_TRACE=0 (the load B configuration). Both overlays refuse the E29 default; apply them on scripts/node/reference/baseline-20260925-e28b.env to reproduce the measured loads.
summary: E28b plus two flagged boundary changes that leave interior k=7 decode steps unchanged. VLLM_E29_END_DRAIN=1 stops the async scheduler from dispatching another speculative step for a request whose step in flight may already reach max_tokens; the vendor guard skips only when completion is certain, so with seven drafts a length-capped request usually ends with one useless verification step that the next request waits behind. VLLM_E29_IDLE_COALESCE_MS keeps collecting requests for a fixed window after the first arrival at an idle engine, so requests released together are prefilled in one step. VLLM_E29_TRACE=1 logs arrivals, dispatches, retirements, holds and resumes.

scheduler.py.change: The E27c scheduler mounted by E28b plus scheduler.patch, additions only: next to the vendor length guard, a non-prefill running request with output placeholders is skipped for this step when committed outputs plus placeholders reach max_tokens (equivalently C + 1 >= N + M under C = N + O + P - 1). Other requests stay schedulable, the request resumes once the pending output shows it still needs tokens, and EOS or stop handling is unchanged. With VLLM_E29_END_DRAIN unset or 0 the file behaves as the parent.

core.py.change: The serving image's engine core plus core.patch, additions only: after an idle engine takes its first ADD, _process_input_queue keeps taking inputs until one fixed deadline VLLM_E29_IDLE_COALESCE_MS later (0-5 ms; 0 = vendor loop), stopping early on shutdown, pause or no runnable request; it refuses a nonzero window with data parallelism. VLLM_E29_TRACE=1 logs enqueue, dispatch, retirement and coalescing times on one monotonic clock.

flags.VLLM_E29_IDLE_COALESCE_MS: 0 in load A (delta.env); 4 in load B (delta-b.env), covering the 3.17 ms maximum arrival spread of 21 cohorts measured in load A
flags.VLLM_E29_TRACE: 1 in load A; 0 in load B and in every Rigmark suite

evidence: Live E28b diagnosis on 2026-09-25 with the frozen Rigmark client: an isolated 256-token C1 reached its first token in 0.339 s and a replay issued 5 s after its cold in 0.840/0.835/1.613 s at 8K/32K/64K, while a request submitted as soon as another finished waited 0.39-0.48 s. Over 40 length-capped predecessors, the next request took 0.333-0.338 s when the predecessor's last step emitted one token (vendor guard fired) and 0.388-0.439 s otherwise. Rigmark issues C1 rounds and each warm replay immediately after the previous request.
expected_cost: A request whose held step falls short is scheduled after that output instead of overlapping it: one scheduling bubble near max_tokens, possibly repeated after further rejections. An isolated request at an idle engine waits up to the coalescing window.
not_included: Cancelling or preempting work already dispatched to the workers, and any change to EOS-finished requests.
